summary: Fix remote CI regression: `node scripts/verify-c2.mjs` threw `TypeError: Cannot open database because the directory does not exist` on a clean checkout because `new Database(DATABASE_PATH)` was called before the parent `apps/server/data/` directory existed. `better-sqlite3` requires the file parent directory to exist when opening. `scripts/verify-c2.mjs` now self-bootstraps: imports `mkdirSync` from `node:fs` and `dirname` from `node:path`, then calls `mkdirSync(dirname(DATABASE_PATH), { recursive: true })` immediately before `new Database(DATABASE_PATH)`. The parent dir is computed programmatically from `DATABASE_PATH` (no hardcoding of `apps/server/data`). Existing cleanup at end (`rmSync(DATABASE_PATH, ...)` plus -shm/-wal) is unchanged; temp db still removed on every run. `mkdirSync` with `recursive:true` is idempotent, so local Windows runs that already have the dir are unaffected.

diffs.verify_c2_mjs: Net +5 lines: +1 import mkdirSync, +1 import dirname, +1 mkdir call, +2-line comment; placed immediately before legacyDatabase is opened at line 91. Existing end-of-script rmSync cleanup preserved verbatim.

root_cause: Line 91 `const legacyDatabase = new Database(DATABASE_PATH)` opens an SQLite file at `apps/server/data/verify-c2-<ts>.db`. `better-sqlite3` `new Database` throws `TypeError: Cannot open database because the directory does not exist` if the file parent dir does not exist. On Windows local dev `apps/server/data` was created by prior runs / the dev server; on a clean CI checkout it does not exist, so the verifier crashed before any test ran. The spawned server `DATABASE_PATH` env points at the same path, so its parent must also exist - covered by the same `mkdirSync`.
fix: Compute parent programmatically via `dirname(DATABASE_PATH)` and `mkdirSync(parent, { recursive: true })` immediately before `new Database(DATABASE_PATH)` at line 91. Parent is NOT hardcoded - derived from the existing `DATABASE_PATH` const. Existing end-of-script `rmSync` cleanup is preserved verbatim.
